Chapter 6: Integrating the Five Practices—Building a Management Flywheel
Now that we’ve laid out the five core management practices, let’s talk about how they come together—almost like pieces of a puzzle that lock in and keep each other turning. Instead of thinking about these practices as isolated moves, imagine them as a kind of management flywheel.
You know how a flywheel works, right? Once it gets going, every little push makes it spin faster and smoother. That’s what happens when a manager makes listening, giving feedback, supporting growth, and nurturing culture part of everyday leadership. The team’s energy starts to build on itself, trust deepens, and suddenly, what used to feel like uphill battles get a whole lot easier.
Here’s how this flywheel effect really kicks in:
Repetition—those small, positive actions you repeat day after day? They become second nature, setting the tone for how your team works together.
Reinforcement—each practice actually feeds the others. When you truly listen, your feedback hits home. That feedback points the way for growth, and a strong culture lifts everything you do.
And then there’s resilience. When things get tough, the trust and habits you’ve built act like shock absorbers, helping your team bounce back instead of breaking.
Let me give you a real-world example. Imagine a nonprofit team suddenly facing a big funding cut. Because their manager had already put in the work—regular check-ins, honest feedback—the team felt safe talking through hard options. What could’ve been a crisis turned into a chance for growth, because that positive culture kept everyone focused on what mattered most.
That’s the flywheel at work: good management habits keep the team moving forward, even when things get rough.
So, try picturing this system like a circle, not a ladder. There’s no end point—just a steady loop of support and improvement. The secret? Keep the flywheel spinning, especially when stress levels rise. Go back to basics: show up, listen, give feedback, support your team’s growth, and nurture the culture.
That’s how you build momentum that lasts, no matter what challenges come your way.
